'''Constantin Corduneanu''' (July 26, 1928 &ndash; December 26, 2018) was a Romanian-American mathematician and professor of mathematics at the [[University of Texas at Arlington]]. In 2015, he was elected a titular member of the [[Romanian Academy]]; he was a corresponding member of the Academy since 1974.<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor emeritus Corduneanu remembered for kindness, contributions to mathematics|publisher=College of Science, The University of Texas at Arlington|url=https://www.uta.edu/science/news/2019/01-29-professor-emeritus-corduneanu-remembered-for-kindness-contributions-to-mathematics.php|website=www.uta.edu|access-date=2021-05-05|archive-date=2021-05-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505133756/https://www.uta.edu/science/news/2019/01-29-professor-emeritus-corduneanu-remembered-for-kindness-contributions-to-mathematics.php|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Mahdavi">{{cite journal |last1=Mahdavi |first1=Mehran |title=A Memorial Tribute to Professor Constantin Corduneanu, The Outstanding Mathematician |journal=Nonautonomous Dynamical Systems |date=1 January 2020 |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=140–150 |doi=10.1515/msds-2020-0115|doi-access=free|mr=4171130 }}</ref><ref name="Octogon">{{cite journal|title=In Memoriam Constantin Corduneanu |url=https://www.uni-miskolc.hu/~matsefi/Octogon/volumes/octogon_2019_1_Constantin_Cordeneanu.pdf|journal=Octogon Mathematical Magazine|volume= 27|issue=1|year= 2019|pages=436–437|first=Mihály|last=Bencze}}</ref><ref name="Nonlinear">{{cite journal|
last1=Aleksandrov|first1= A. Yu.| last2=Martynyuk|first2= A. A.|last3=Pavel|first3= N. H.|last4= Vassilyev|first4= S. N.
|title=Professor Constantin Corduneanu |url=https://www.e-ndst.kiev.ua/v12n2/0(39).pdf|journal=Nonlinear Dynamics and Systems Theory|volume=12|issue=2|year=2012|pages=111–118|mr=2962102}}</ref>

==Biography==
Corduneanu was born in [[Potângeni]], [[Iași County]], the son of Aglaea and Costache Corduneanu.<ref name="Octogon"/> From 1940 to 1947, he attended military high school in [[Iași]] and [[Predeal]]. In 1951, he graduated from the Faculty of Sciences of the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]], Department of Mathematics.<ref name="EVZ">{{cite news|url=https://evz.ro/zi-neagra-pentru-romania-doliu.html|title=Zi neagră pentru România. Doliu pentru toată comunitatea științifică românească. Un ilustru român a murit|lang=ro| newspaper=[[Evenimentul Zilei]]|date=December 27, 2018|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref> His teachers there included [[Alexander Myller]], [[Octav Mayer]], {{ill|Mendel Haimovici|ro}}, {{ill|Dimitrie Mangeron|ro}}, [[Ilie Popa (mathematician)|Ilie Popa]], {{ill|Gheorghe Gheorghiev|ro}}, {{ill|Alexandru Climescu|ro}}, {{ill|Ion L. Creangă|ro}}, and {{ill|Adolf Haimovici|ro}}.<ref name="Adevărul">{{cite news|url=https://adevarul.ro/stiri-interne/societate/am-contribuit-la-pregatirea-a-peste-7000-de-768522.html|title="Am contribuit la pregătirea a peste 7000 de studenți"|lang=ro|newspaper=[[Adevărul]]|date=December 5, 2006|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref> Corduneanu received his Ph.D. in 1956 from the University of Iași with thesis ''Probleme globale pentru ecuațiile diferențiale de ordin I și II'' written under the supervision of Ilie Popa.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=34269}}</ref> The thesis defense the committee was composed of [[Miron Nicolescu]], [[Grigore Moisil]], and {{ill|Nicolae-Victor Teodorescu|lt=Nicolae Teodorescu|ro|Nicolae-Victor Teodorescu}}.<ref name="Nonlinear"/> 

From 1949 to 1977 he was a faculty member at the University of Iași, advancing in rank to full professor, and serving as Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics (1968–1972) and [[List of academic ranks|pro-rector]] (1972–1973 and 1974–1977).<ref name="EVZ"/> He also held faculty positions at the [[Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iași]] and at the [[Ștefan cel Mare University of Suceava|University of Suceava]], where he served as [[Rector (academia)|rector]] from 1966 to 1968.<ref name="EVZ"/><ref name="Mahdavi"/>

In 1977, Corduneanu decided to leave Romania. He first went to [[Italy]], where he taught some courses at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Trieste]].<ref name="Mahdavi"/> In January 1978, he emigrated to the United States, and secured a teaching position at the [[University of Rhode Island]] (where he had been a visiting professor in 1967–1968 and 1973–1974). After spending a year as visiting professor at the [[University of Tennessee]] at [[Knoxville]], he became a tenured professor in the fall of 1979 at the University of Texas at Arlington,<ref name="Mahdavi"/> where he taught until his retirement in 1996.<ref name="EVZ"/> He died at Medical City [[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]] in 2018, at age 90.<ref name="Octogon"/>

A Festschrift in his honor, titled ''Mathematical Analysis With Applications'', was published in 2018.
